programme: No coherent module. The concordant set splits into unrelated developmental and housekeeping programmes: a paraxial-mesoderm/neural-crest triad (PAX3, PAX7, TCF15 — satellite-cell and neural-crest specification, with PAX4 a pancreatic paralog sharing only the PAX DNA-binding fold, not the pathway), a lung/thyroid epithelial identity factor (NKX2-1), a hematopoietic/mast-cell factor (GATA2), a macrophage lipid-sensing nuclear receptor (NR1H3), a germline-restricted CTCF paralog (CTCFL), a general transcriptional corepressor (CTBP2), an intestinal-crypt/Wnt factor (ASCL2), and two chromatin remodelers from different complexes (PBRM1 in PBAF, SMARCA1 in ISWI). None of these groupings converges on one process that a biologist could point to as running in both blood and skin.
role_in_a: Not answerable at the module level — GATA2, NR1H3 and NKX2-1 each have isolated, disease-adjacent roles in COVID-19 (immune deficiency/HLH, placental lipid handling, alveolar epithelial transcriptional identity) but they are not parts of one axis.
role_in_b: Not answerable at the module level — the only retrieved psoriasis hit (GATA2/GDF15/neutrophil paper) is a single tangential association, and none of the remaining factors have any documented psoriasis role.
shared_axis: No mechanism ties these factors together as a set. The developmental/myogenic block (PAX3, PAX7, TCF15, PAX4) has no established or plausible role in either an antiviral blood response or a keratinocyte-driven skin disease, and the remaining factors belong to at least four unrelated pathways (hematopoiesis, lipid sensing, chromatin remodeling, germline chromatin insulation) rather than one shared programme.
reasoning: Twelve factors recurring across patient-group comparisons is a statistical fact, not a mechanism; here they fail to cluster into any named complex or pathway, half have no Open Targets association with either disease, and the retrieved papers are almost all off-topic (ovarian cancer for CTCFL, pig organoids for PAX4, placental pathology for NR1H3). Forcing a story would mean picking 2-3 factors and ignoring the rest, which the exercise explicitly warns against.
support: PMID 42130790 — GATA2 in a COVID-19-associated HLH case report, not a mechanistic disease link; PMID 40153067 — GATA2 haploinsufficiency as a rare susceptibility factor for critical COVID-19, an inherited-deficiency finding rather than evidence of a shared regulatory programme; PMID 36049542 — GATA2 appears in a psoriasis/GDF15/neutrophil model but the abstract does not establish GATA2 as a driver; PMID 42202512 — NR1H3 linked to lipid metabolism in SARS-CoV-2 placentitis, a distinct clinical entity from COVID-19 proper; PMID 37523502 — NKX2-1 appears in a lung single-cell atlas of COVID-19 BAL, reflecting alveolar cell identity rather than a regulatory link to psoriasis.
how_to_falsify: Take the three factors with any disease-adjacent literature (GATA2, NR1H3, NKX2-1) and test whether they co-occupy shared enhancers or physically interact in a myeloid/mast-cell context using ChIP-seq or Hi-C in PBMCs from COVID-19 patients and lesional skin from psoriasis patients; absence of shared binding sites or co-regulated target genes across the two tissues would confirm there is no real cross-disease programme, consistent with this call.
caveats: 32 patient-group comparisons across 4 independent cohort pairs is a reasonably large base for the recurrence statistic, but recurrence measures reproducibility of network inference, not biological relevance. Psoriasis-side annotation was queried only under 'Psoriasiform dermatitis,' which likely explains the near-total absence of Open Targets and literature hits for that disease and should not be read as true absence of any TF-disease relationship. Tissue-generic factors (CEBPB, E2F1/3, KLF1, PBX1, FOXO1/3, TAL1, AR, BCL6, CEBPD, NFATC2) were already removed, so the temptation to invoke a generic myeloid or interferon master regulator should be resisted — none remain in this list to build such a story on.
